summary: Specifies the Time protocol, which gives a site-independent, machine readable date and time as seconds since midnight on January first 1900. It is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it.

eli5.summary: A computer tells another computer the time as one big number, counting seconds from the start of 1900.

questions: what port does the time protocol use
when does the rfc 868 time value run out
subtitle: A service on port 37 that returns the time as a 32-bit count of seconds since 1900.

tldr.problem: Not every system has a clock, and all clocks can be wrong, so hosts need a way to confirm or correct their idea of the time from independent sites.
tldr.mechanism: A server on port 37 returns a 32-bit binary number: the seconds since midnight on 1 January 1900 GMT. It does this over TCP and then closes, or in a single UDP reply to an empty datagram.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is an Internet Standard for hosts that choose to implement it. It says the 1900 base will serve until the year 2036.

today: RFC 868 is an Internet Standard and has not been obsoleted or updated, so it remains the definition of the Time Protocol.

sections.title: A Machine-Readable Time Service
sections.content:
RFC 868 defines the Time Protocol, which provides a site-independent, machine readable date and time. The server sends back to the originating source the time in seconds since midnight on 1 January 1900.

One motivation is that not all systems have a date/time clock, and all are subject to occasional human or machine error. With time servers, a system can quickly confirm or correct its idea of the time by making a brief poll of several independent sites on the network.
sections.eli5: Some computers have no clock, and clocks can be wrong. So a computer can ask a few others what time it is and check.

sections.title: Using TCP and UDP
sections.content:
The protocol may run above TCP or UDP, always on port 37 (45 octal). Over TCP, the server listens, the user connects, the server sends the time as a 32-bit binary number and closes, and the user receives it and closes. If the server cannot determine the time, it should either refuse the connection or close it without sending anything.

Over UDP, the user sends an empty datagram to port 37 and the server replies with a datagram containing the 32-bit time. If the server cannot determine the time, it should discard the arriving datagram and make no reply.
sections.eli5: You knock on door number 37, and the machine hands back one number, the time, and that is all.

sections.title: The Time Value
sections.content:
The time is the number of seconds since 00:00 (midnight) 1 January 1900 GMT, so that the time 1 is 12:00:01 am on 1 January 1900 GMT. The RFC says this base will serve until the year 2036.

Examples from the RFC: 2,208,988,800 corresponds to 00:00 1 Jan 1970 GMT, 2,398,291,200 to 00:00 1 Jan 1976 GMT, 2,524,521,600 to 00:00 1 Jan 1980 GMT, and 2,629,584,000 to 00:00 1 May 1983 GMT. The value -1,297,728,000 corresponds to 00:00 17 Nov 1858 GMT.
sections.eli5: It is like counting every second since the start of 1900 on a giant stopwatch. The number gets big, but it tells you exactly when you are.
